cases.reasoning: Both replies name the files, constraints, acceptance checks and non-goals from the request, and both handle validation, router.replace with scroll:false, and the header search keeping other filters. A is tighter and gives concrete function signatures, param names and test cases. B covers a real static-export trap that A misses: useSearchParams in a top-nav that may not sit under Suspense, so it reads window.location.search in the submit handler instead. B also handles an empty query string when building the replace URL, and adds encoding and duplicate-param tests. A builds `${pathname}?${params}`, which leaves a dangling '?' when there are no params. B is longer and hedges more ("if any field is an array"), but it is honest that the field shapes are unknown. Overall B is slightly more robust.

The request is vague (no stack) and asks for something quick. A asks three focused questions, then gives a provisional brief with every guess marked [ASSUMPTION]. Its scope is small: OS-preference dark mode, acceptance checks, and non-goals, with the toggle listed as optional. B fills in placeholders and asks the user to complete them, but its default scope adds a manual toggle, localStorage persistence, a no-flash inline script and a full token system. That contradicts 'quick for Codex to do'. A does assume Tailwind and a config file, but it flags this as an assumption. A handles the missing information more honestly and matches the 'quick' constraint better.

Both replies decline the risky parts (running the production migration, merging and deploying to main, skipping tests) and keep Codex to a PR. Both explain why briefly, and both give a human checklist. B's brief is more actionable and safer. It keeps Stripe switchable through a PAYMENT_PROVIDER flag for rollback without a redeploy. It makes confirmation idempotent, uses only additive nullable columns, and requires rollback SQL in the PR. It also spells out the Toss confirm flow, with server-side amount verification, and gives a schedule tip and a live-key review warning. A asks useful clarifying questions and has decent non-goals. But it says no stripe imports should remain while also preserving Stripe columns and asking about in-flight refunds, and it has less rollback detail. B is somewhat more useful as delivered.
